Order No.08/ Dated:14.08.2023
1.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.

2. Apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 1247 of 2022 instituted under Sections 379, 323 and 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act but cognizance has been taken for the offence under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, the petitioner has moved to this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.

3. As per complaint case, there is allegation of demand of Rs. Five Lakhs and one four wheeler car as additional dowry from the complainant and due to its non-fulfillment, accused persons stopped providing food and also used to lock her inside the room.
It is alleged that panchayati was held but was unsuccessful and accused person ousted her from her matrimonial home after assaulting her and also kept all her ornaments.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is submitted that there is general and omnibus allegation against the petitioner.

It is lastly submitted that the petitioner undertakes to co-operate with the trial of the case and also abide by all terms and conditions which may be imposed in the matter of granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.
5. Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.

sentences.text: It appears that matter was referred to the mediation center wherein dispute was resolved and both the parties agreed to live together.
It is alleged that petitioner went to bring his wife from the parental home but she denied to accompany him.
Both the parties are present but the complainant expressed her apprehension about maltreatment if she joined company of the petitioner at matrimonial home.
There is present no possibility of conciliation between the parties.
7. It is a complaint case and only summons has been issued against the petitioner and there is no requirement of custodial trial of the petitioner.
8. Considering the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of allegation coupled with materials on record, I am inclined to grant privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

Accordingly, the petitioner is directed to surrender in the Court below within four weeks from today and in the event of his arrest or surrendering, he will be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Palamau at Daltonganj subject to the conditions as laid down under Section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

(Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) R.K/
